_comment: Layout, sizing and typography for the header, the site footer and the sticky action bar. Colours arrive through the Figma mirror (colors/top-and-footer); everything here is measured off the artwork. VERIFIED against Figma component set `header-bar-mobile` (14924:2118), instance `footer-mobile` (page ↳ footer), and the page template `Guidline-UI Template › Layout` (23430:298541) on 2026-08-19.

_source.measured: Every dimension below was read off the Figma node named in _binding. Figma V.7.1 has no dimension variables, so fixed pixel values stay verbatim rather than being rounded onto the spacing scale.
_source.header-phoenix-opacity: 70%, read off the `Logo 1` node in every variant. The first build used semantic.opacity.muted (40%) because the Frontend renders its own copy at `opacity-40` — that was a guess from the wrong source and it was wrong. No semantic opacity role carries 70, so the literal stands until one exists.
_source.action-*: The sticky action bar has no Figma component set — it exists only as a frame drawn inside the page template, and as `components/common/footer-button` in the Frontend (17 call sites). Values are measured from the template drawing; the two-button layout comes from the Frontend, which Figma has not drawn.
_source.footer-shadow: storybook-local. Figma stacks two drop shadows on the contact chips; design.md has no elevation role with two layers at these radii, so the value is stated here.
_source.header-appbar-gap: Figma's `Frame 1000012514` inside `appbar-main` uses a 12px gap between the right-hand items. The app bar's own row is SPACE_BETWEEN, so it has no gap of its own.
_source.header-wordmark-*: Figma's `heading` frame holds `Frame 1000012509` at 358x32, which holds the 246x31 wordmark. The row is one pixel taller than the artwork, and that pixel is the difference between a 146px header and a 145px one.
_source.device-*: iPhone 16 in logical points — 393x852, corner radius 47. Figma's template frames are 390x844, an iPhone 14-class canvas, so a mock at real iPhone 16 size is 3pt wider and 8pt taller than the Figma frame. That difference lands entirely in the `main` slot, which is what a responsive shell is supposed to do.
_source.header-phoenix-blend: Figma composites the watermark with HARD_LIGHT, not normal blending. Without it the bird reads as a flat lighter red instead of catching the gradient behind it. CSS has the same mode, so this is a direct translation rather than an approximation.
_source.header-*-phoenix-right / -bottom: Negative offsets: the watermark deliberately bleeds past the header's right and bottom edges and is clipped. Measured against each variant's own frame — home overflows 32 right / 18 bottom, success 32 / 35. The sub-page variant hides it entirely.
_source.header-sub-padding-y / header-sub-title-: Re-read 2026-08-21, third reading of this frame. The designer switched every variant of the set to hug and moved the padding onto the bar: type=sub-page is now HORIZONTAL with 16 on all four sides, an 8 gap, and a `heading` column FIXED at 36 holding a 24px line centred vertically — 16 + 36 + 16 = 68, where it read 56 the day before. The 16 that used to sit on the `heading` frame is now the bar's own padding-y, so the token moved with it and `header-sub-heading-padding-y` is gone. The 36-tall box is also what stops Thai ink from clipping without CSS having to grow the line box by hand: a 24px line inside a 36px box leaves 6 above and below, which is more than the 4.8 an ascender-heavy Thai glyph runs past its baseline.
_source.header-home-padding-top: 16, up from 8, changed by the designer on 2026-08-21 in the same pass that switched the frames to hug. The 8px reading was correct when it was taken; the top and bottom paddings are no longer a matched pair on this variant (16 top, 32 bottom) and neither is derivable from the other. Worth noting that the height alone would not have caught this: minHeight 154 with an 8px top padding still measures 154 in the browser, it just puts the extra 8 in the wrong place. The padding had to be read, not inferred from the total.
_source.header-home-height / header-success-heig: 154 and 96, both hug now. Every variant of `header-bar-mobile` was FIXED and is AUTO on its primary axis as of 2026-08-21, so the frame is whatever its own content adds up to. home: 16 + appbar 36 + gap 16 + heading 54 (a 32 wordmark row over a 22 slogan line) + 32 = 154, where the FIXED frame said 146 and cropped 8 off the bottom padding. success: 16 + Head 64 + 16 = 96, and its `appbar-main` is hidden so it contributes nothing — this closes the 94-vs-96 gap recorded the day before, in the direction the library had already rendered.
_source.profile-*: Measured off `header-bar-profile-moblie` (14962:94338), all 9 variants, on 2026-08-19. 72 tall with 16 of side padding; a 56px avatar beside a stack with 2 of vertical padding and a 6 gap; name 16/24 Semibold with a 20px chevron; the meta row 12/18 Regular with a 4 gap. The show/hide pill is 20 tall, radius full, filled `colors/profile/profile-fg-dark-red`. The notification variant swaps the 36px button well for a 32px glyph with a 16px white badge carrying a 10/18 count.
_source.header-action-border-width: 1px, and it is the same stroke on all three action wells — but Figma switches its `visible` flag off on exactly one: the back arrow on type=sub-page (14924:3521). The hamburger keeps it on both type=sub-page (14924:5615) and type=home-page (21282:140842). Read on 2026-08-20 after the border was drawn on the back arrow too; the first read took strokeWeight and cornerRadius and never looked at strokes[0].visible. Rendered as an inset box-shadow rather than a CSS border because Figma's strokeAlign is INSIDE — it paints over the 36px frame instead of taking 2px out of it, which under border-box would leave the 24px glyph only 22px to sit in.
_source.status-bar-padding-x: 32. The status bar's own inset, wider than the header's 16 because the time and the indicators clear the rounded corners. Taken from the AppShell story that drew this by hand before it was a component.
_source.status-bar-*: Measured off the StatusBar instance inside `[Mobile] Profile` (22483:144307) on 2026-08-21, variant `Dark Mode=True, Type=Default`. 390x47 filled with the brand red. The cut-out is a NOTCH — 156x33, black, centred at x=117 and pulled 2 above the top edge — not a Dynamic Island. An earlier version of this file guessed an Island at 125x37 because the device tokens say iPhone 16; Figma draws the iPhone 14-class notch, and Figma is what the design was made against. Time sits at x=27 y=14 in a 54x21 box. The indicators end 26 from the right: signal 18x12 at x=286, wifi 17x11.8 at x=312, battery 27.4x13 at x=336 — an 8 gap between signal and wifi, 7 between wifi and battery.
_source.profile-summary-*: `header-profile` (15006:92124, one variant type=default): 390x187, 16 of padding, filled with the brand red and rounded 24 on its BOTTOM corners only. Inside it, stacked with no gap: a 358x80 card rounded 16/16/0/0 with a 3px gold top edge (#EAB308, INSIDE) holding a `nokcash-profile` instance; a 358x1 `Line`; and a 358x74 card rounded 0/0/16/16, SPACE_BETWEEN, holding three `summary-icon-profile` instances. 16 + 80 + 1 + 74 + 16 = 187, and the block hugs.
_source.profile-summary-rule-*: The `Line` (15006:91697) is 358x1 with a 1px WHITE dashed 4/4 stroke on its top edge and no fill of its own — so the row is one pixel of the block's red showing through, with white dashes painted over it. What a reader sees is a red dashed line, because the dashes are the part that is NOT red. The first build translated this as a white dashed border on a white card and it rendered as nothing at all, which is how a divider can be present in the code, correct in its colour, and invisible on screen. The frame also carries paddingTop 16 and itemSpacing 4, both inert: it is FIXED at 1 tall with no children, so neither can do anything. The 16 was modelled as `profile-summary-rule-gap` and drawn as real space, which pushed the lower card 16 down; it is gone. Read 2026-08-21.
_source.profile-summary-no-border-on-the-lower-c: The lower card has `strokes: []` — no border on any side. An earlier reading recorded a 1px white border all round, taken from strokeTopWeight/strokeRightWeight etc., which report 1 on every frame whether or not a stroke exists to weigh. The paint list is what says a stroke is there; the weights only say how thick it would be. Same trap as the action-well border on the header, one axis over.
_source.profile-summary-frontend-gap: The Frontend has none of this — `profile-header-card` is one plain white card on the page background. Building /profile from the Frontend alone is what produced the wrong shape.
_source.header-success-*: The success meta row (label + value) sits on legacy 14/24 styles no role carries — see _unmigrated_type. Confirmed correct as drawn; literals until a role exists.
_source.subtitle-removed: Figma's sub-page variant draws a hidden subtitle layer (งวดวันที่ …, 14/24 Medium). The product never shows it — decided with the user 2026-08-21 — so the component does not model it and its literals left with it. If the product ever grows a draw date under the title, this is the layer to re-read: header-bar-mobile > type=sub-page > heading, the hidden TEXT under text-center.
_source.header-success-title: typography/display/xl-semb — 20/36 Semibold. The layer carried a legacy 22/34 style until 2026-08-21, when the designer restyled it to the same role the new type4 title uses. An earlier binding here read title/lg/semibold (16/24), chosen before the restyle; re-read off the layer's own style id and corrected.
_source.profile-padding-y: 8 — added by the designer in Figma on 2026-08-21; the variant now carries padding 8/16/8/16 and the bar stays 72. Re-read off 14962:94338 the same day.
_source.profile-meta: The member-id row carries the text style `typography/caption/l-reg` — read off the layer's own style id on 2026-08-21. The overlay used to bind label/md/regular, picked because its numbers matched (12/18 mobile, 14 desktop on both roles). Same values, wrong word: the binding is vocabulary, and Figma's own style name is the vocabulary that counts. Why the row 'looks big' in Storybook: both roles are responsive on the VIEWPORT, so a desktop browser shows the 14px desktop step even inside a 393px phone mock — the phone itself shows 12. A container-query migration would fix the mock; noted, not done.
_source.header-main-*: `type=type4` (23625:34736), added to the set by the designer on 2026-08-21 and read the same day: 390x68, HORIZONTAL, 16 of padding, an 8 gap, brand red, no phoenix. A `heading` column on the left holding `main-title` at typography/display/xl-semb (20/36 Semibold, left-aligned, white), and `appbar-main` on the right holding the two counters and the 36px action well. Both sides grow, so the title takes whatever the counters leave. This is the shape the Frontend calls `big_title` and draws at 96; Figma says 68 and Figma is the authority.

_unmigrated_type._note: Two text layers in header-bar-mobile still use pre-token styles, both on the success variant's meta row. Their 14/24 pairs are correct as drawn (confirmed by the user 2026-08-21) — no existing role carries 14/24, so they stay literals until Phase 2 grows one. The success title was resolved the other way on the same day: its 22/34 layer is stale, the intended role is title/lg/semibold (16/24), and the overlay now binds that role — Figma's text layer catches up in Phase 2. Keyed by token name for check-typography.py.
_unmigrated_type.header-success-meta-line-height: 24px — same pair, confirmed correct as drawn 2026-08-21

_figma_icons._comment: The icons Figma actually instantiates, per node, read on 2026-08-20 (14924:2118) and 2026-08-21 (14962:94338). check-figma-icons.py asserts the icons used in `sources` are exactly this set -- an extra one fails as loudly as a missing one. check-icons.py only ever asked whether a name resolved, and a wrong-but-real icon passes that: three of the five under 14924:2118 were wrong for months because resolving is not matching. Keys prefixed with `_` are documented but not enforced, which is how an icon Figma draws inside a nested component -- and that the nested component already renders -- is recorded without being demanded of the parent's source.

icons.outline-NokPoints-W: type=home-page > appbar-main > Frame 1000012514 > counter 1, icons-size Size=24 Colors=On BG (21282:140832). Was filled-empty-wallet at 16px. Same counter appears on type=type4.
icons.outline-Lottery: same row, counter 2 (21282:140837). Was filled-Lottery at 16px. Same counter appears on type=type4.
icons.filled-navigation: icon-right on type=home-page (21282:140842) and type=sub-page (14924:5615), inside button Size=M Type=Tertiary. The hamburger is a real icon in the set; the stories drew it by hand as three divs, and sub-page carried outline-notification instead. Also icon-right on type=type4 (23625:34736).
icons.arrow-left-L: icon-left on type=sub-page, inside button Size=M Type=Tertiary (14924:3521).

icons._comment: Read on 2026-08-21 by walking all 9 variants and resolving every INSTANCE through getMainComponentAsync. Filtering that walk on `parent.name === 'icons'` is what the first pass did, and it is wrong twice over: it drops arrow-right-S, whose main component has no parent at all, and it keeps filled-user, which Figma draws inside the avatar instance rather than in this component.
icons.arrow-right-S: Frame 44487 > Frame 44466 > Frame 44468 > icon+size Size=20 > arrows/arrow-right-S (main 14291:133085), 20x20. Drawn on the five signed-in variants and on none of the four no-log-in ones, whose Frame 44468 holds the greeting alone. It is a real instance, not the raw VECTOR it was taken for -- its main component simply sits outside the `icons` frame and reports parent === null, so a walk keyed on that frame cannot see it.
icons.outline-eye: Frame 44467 > button > icons-size Size=12 Colors=On BG (14513:65) > outline-eye (14291:110971), 12x12. The pill's rest glyph: state=login+no-active, login+actived, login+noti-1 and login-noti-2.
icons.outline-eye-off: same slot on state=login+view (instance 22535:139053), where the pill reads 'ซ่อน' because the id is already revealed.
icons.outline-document-copy: Frame 44467 > icons-size Size=16 Colors=On BG (14513:67) > outline-document-copy (14291:110979), 16x16, sitting between the id text and the pill on the row's own 4 gap. Figma draws it on state=login+view; state=login+no-active carries the same node with visible=false and state=login+actived omits it. Absent from the source entirely until now, which is why the id could be shown but never copied.
icons.filled-navigation: icon-right > button Size=M Type=Tertiary (14291:130982) > icons-size Size=24 Colors=Secondary > filled-navigation (14291:110831), 24x24. The hamburger on state=login+no-active, login+view and no-log-in+no-actived.
icons.filled-close: the same 36px well and the same 24px icons-size slot, on state=login+actived (16309:11321) and state=no-log-in+actived (16309:11364): Figma's `actived` axis is the menu being open, and it swaps the hamburger for a close glyph. The source drew the hamburger in both, so the open menu had no way to close itself.
icons.outline-notification: icon-right > icons-size Size=32 Colors=On BG (14513:73) > outline-notification (14971:123243), 32x32, beside a 16px Badge frame. Every type=nokplus variant. This well has no button wrapper -- the glyph and the badge sit in icon-right directly.
icons._filled-user: Frame 44487 > avatar > Avata > icons-size Size=16 Colors=Primary (14510:23233) > filled-user (14291:111058), rendered at 22x22. Recorded because the walk surfaces it, and underscored because it is not this component's to draw: it belongs to the Type=Guest avatar (14291:133628), and Avatar.tsx already draws it. Naming it in ProfileHeader.tsx would duplicate Avatar's decision, so the equality check must not demand it here.

_corrections.phoenix-opacity: Was 40% (semantic.opacity.muted, taken from the Frontend). Figma says 70%.
_corrections.phoenix-blend: Was missing. Figma composites it with HARD_LIGHT.
_corrections.phoenix-geometry: Was one square `size` positioned with a percentage translate. Figma gives each variant its own box and offset, and the success one is 118x125 — not square.

_figma_gaps._closed-2026-08-21-success-frame-was-two: CLOSED. type=success (22447:63726) was FIXED at 94 while its own auto-layout added up to 96; the library rendered 96 and recorded the disagreement rather than clipping a line the design asks for. The designer switched the frame to hug the same day and it now reports 96, which is what the library was already drawing. Kept as a record of how the gap was resolved, not as an open item.
_figma_gaps.profile-variants-disagree-on-their-own-p: `header-bar-profile-moblie` (14962:94338) has 9 variants, all 72 tall. One — type=lottery, state=login+no-active (14962:91594) — hugs with padding 8/16/8/16. The other eight are FIXED 72 with padding 0/16/0/16 and centre their 56-tall content, which lands in the same place, so nothing renders differently and the library models the padded one. It is still one variant edited and eight not: if the content ever grows, eight frames clip and one does not. A designer applies 8/16 to the rest. Read 2026-08-21.
